speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with agitation and jaundice, which suggests a significant underlying issue. To begin our assessment, have you recently experienced any abdominal pain, changes in urine or stool color, or a history of alcohol use?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hepatitis likely due to Cocaine/Ecstasy toxicity, high-risk sexual exposure (Hepatitis B/C or HIV), or acute alcoholic hepatitis; further testing required to confirm etiology and rule out other causes.

REQUEST TEST: Liver function panel (AST, ALT, Bilirubin, Alkaline Phosphatase, GGT), Coagulation profile (PT/INR), Hepatitis serologies (A, B, C), HIV test, and Urinalysis.

REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound.
